caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: DANDI:001272
attempts.paper_title: Excitation and polarization of isolated neurons by high-frequency sine waves for temporal interference stimulation
attempts.entry_title: Excitation of isolated neurons by high-frequency sine waves (Semenov et al. 2025)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Semenov, Kim, Silkuniene and Pakhomov (2025) on dandiset 001272, which holds the Di-8-ANEPPS control recordings of Figure S1 (three neurons stimulated with 250-ms, 2-kHz sine waves), and the paper's FluoVolt findings on its other deposits, 001030, 001032, 001033, 001035 and 001271 (Figures 1 to 3 and S2), and fits the strobe imaging of Figure 4 (001273) without the debris ROI the paper scaled to, which is not deposited.

notebooks.title: Di-8-ANEPPS controls on DANDI:001272, with a FluoVolt reference group
FluoVolt findings on the paper's other deposits
Strobe imaging of membrane charging on DANDI:001273

outcomes.statement: The Di-8-ANEPPS control experiments were made on eight neurons, at field strengths tested in a random sequence.
outcomes.source: Results, Sensitivity to unmodulated sine waves was not caused by FluoVolt dye, paragraph 1; Figure S1
outcomes.quote: Experiments were performed on eight neurons using different electric field strengths tested in a random sequence
outcomes.notes: The dataset holds 3 neurons (subjects 2_20240806, 3_20240806 and 4_20240806, with 20, 29 and 16 sessions), against 8 in the paper, and no frame stack is deposited twice. The fields were tested in mixed order in all three (rises and falls in each); subjects 2 and 4 mostly escalate.

outcomes.statement: With Di-8-ANEPPS, APs appear as brief reductions of emission, opposite in sign to FluoVolt.
outcomes.source: Results, Sensitivity to unmodulated sine waves was not caused by FluoVolt dye, paragraph 1; Methods, Recording of the optical APs and data analyses; Figure S1 legend
outcomes.quote: APs were identified by the reduction instead of the increase of emission
outcomes.notes: Answer to questions/001272.yaml on the O3 width. The claims file now takes an AP's width at half height between 1 and 20 ms, where it had 2 to 20 ms; re-run with 1 ms, the outcome is unchanged. Under all 12 readings (O1 ROI a, b and the whole frame, O2 F0 a and b, O3 height a and b), every neuron with APs had more APs on the inverted trace than on the trace as recorded in all of its sessions with APs. The trace as recorded yields 2 APs, in subject 2 under the four Otsu-ROI readings with the 5% height (none with the 2-ms bound). The largest brief deflection during the stimulus, as recorded, is negative in 57 of 65 sessions.
deviations: The soma outline is not deposited. The claims file's Otsu ROI (O1 a) keeps one bright membrane edge of the soma (26 to 48 of 256 pixels), and eroding it by 2 pixels (O1 b) leaves nothing in all 65 files, so reading (b) equals (a). The whole deposited 16 x 16 frame, a crop around the soma, is run as a third ROI reading.
Frame 0 (1.7 to 15.7 times the median brightness) and the last frame are left out of every trace, a standard choice.

outcomes.statement: Near threshold, 2-kHz sine waves elicited one or a few delayed APs in Di-8-ANEPPS neurons.
outcomes.source: Results, Sensitivity to unmodulated sine waves was not caused by FluoVolt dye, paragraph 1; Figure S1
outcomes.quote: Stimulation near the threshold elicited one or a few delayed APs
outcomes.notes: Under the adopted readings (whole frame, F0 (a), height (b) read as prominence, O5 (a)) every neuron fires a median of 1 AP at its threshold field, but only subject 4 has its first AP 100 ms or more after onset (137 ms); subjects 3 and 2 fire at 63 and 6 ms. So 1 of 3 neurons meets the criterion, where more than half are needed. Each neuron's near-threshold AP is later than its APs at higher fields (2.7, 8.3 and 21.8 ms). With the height as prominence the criterion is met in 20 of 48 reading combinations, 0 of 24 under O5 (a) and 20 of 24 under O5 (b). With the height as the dF value it is met in 19 of 48 (6 of 24 under O5 (a), 13 of 24 under O5 (b); 12 of 48 with the earlier 2-ms width bound); under whole/a/b subject 2 then fires 2 APs at threshold, the first at 108 ms, and subject 4 one at 201 ms, so 2 of 3 neurons meet it. One or a few APs near threshold hold in all three neurons, later than at higher fields, and a delay of 100 ms or more in one or two of the three, depending on the height reading. The questions on "delayed" and on the AP height are for the paper's authors (findings). Changed from partially reproduced after verification round 3. The criterion is one test per neuron, which needs the median near-threshold session to have 1 to 3 APs and its first AP delayed, and it is met when more than half of the neurons pass it; 1 of 3 passes under the adopted readings, under O4 (a) and (b) alike. Partially reproduced described the two halves of that test, which the criterion does not judge apart. Under O5 (b), "delayed" relative to the neuron's own higher fields, every neuron's near-threshold AP is later, so the outcome rests on the reading of "delayed" (assumed true).
deviations: Assumed the AP height read as prominence for Di-8-ANEPPS, after verification round 1. With the height as the dF value, the whole frame and height (b), the detector finds 46 peaks after the stimulus in 23 of 65 sessions (0.91 per 100 ms, against 2.09 during it), as bleaching raises the inverted trace; with prominence it finds 1 (0.02 against 1.43). The value reading is shown beside it.

Assumed O5 (a), a first AP at least 100 ms after onset, as the paper's sense of "delayed". The paper quantifies the near-threshold delay only for FluoVolt (100 to 200 ms, Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz unmodulated sine waves, paragraph 1) and says the Di-8-ANEPPS effects did not differ (Results, Sensitivity to unmodulated sine waves was not caused by FluoVolt dye). Under O5 (b), relative to the neuron's own higher fields, the outcome depends on the ROI and height readings (met in 13 of 24 combinations with the height as the dF value, 20 of 24 as prominence).

outcomes.statement: In Di-8-ANEPPS neurons, increasing the field strength reduced the delay to the first AP and induced sustained firing.
outcomes.source: Results, Sensitivity to unmodulated sine waves was not caused by FluoVolt dye, paragraph 1; Figure S1
outcomes.quote: Increasing the electric field strength reduced the delay and induced sustained firing
outcomes.notes: Under the adopted readings (whole frame, height (b) read as prominence) the first-AP latency correlates negatively with field in all 3 neurons (Spearman rho -0.63, -0.03 and -0.50, p 0.007, 0.88 and 0.058) and all 3 show sustained firing (in 5, 11 and 10 sessions). The criterion is met under 10 of 12 readings and all 6 with height (b), with the height as prominence and as the dF value alike, and with the earlier 2-ms width bound. With the height as the dF value more sessions show sustained firing (8, 22 and 11 under whole/a/b), part of it noise on a raised baseline (null test). Most single correlations are not significant (rho from -0.94 to 0.50 over readings). It fails under the 5% height with the whole-frame ROI, where few Di-8-ANEPPS APs reach 5%.
deviations: Assumed the AP height read as prominence, as for figs1-near-threshold-delayed-aps; the outcome is the same with the height as the dF value.

Assumed O3 height reading (b), 5 SD of the trace before onset, for Di-8-ANEPPS. The 5% level is the Methods' selection level for FluoVolt APs, and the paper says Di-8-ANEPPS has a lower voltage sensitivity (Results, Sensitivity to unmodulated sine waves was not caused by FluoVolt dye); the Di-8-ANEPPS APs measured here have a median height of 3.7 to 6.7% over the readings.

outcomes.statement: In Di-8-ANEPPS neurons, the strongest fields replaced firing with sustained depolarization (excitation followed by inhibition of firing).
outcomes.source: Results, Sensitivity to unmodulated sine waves was not caused by FluoVolt dye, paragraph 1; Figure S1 legend
outcomes.quote: induced sustained firing that culminated in sustained depolarization
outcomes.notes: Answer to questions/001272.yaml on the O3 width. The claims file now takes an AP's width at half height between 1 and 20 ms, where it had 2 to 20 ms; re-run with 1 ms, the outcome is unchanged. At most 1 of the 3 neurons meets the criterion under any of the 24 reading and level combinations (more than half needed), as with 2 ms, and also with the AP height taken as prominence. Subjects 2 and 4 were stimulated up to 234 V/cm only, close to their thresholds (108 to 180 and 108 to 205 V/cm), and never reach sustained depolarization. Subject 3, stimulated up to 504 V/cm, meets it only with the whole frame and the 5% height (with the height as prominence also with the Otsu ROI and level (b)); with the whole frame and height (b) it still fires 6 APs in the last 100 ms at 504 V/cm, with a late inverted dF of 2.9 to 3.3% at 396 to 504 V/cm against 1.4 to 2.4% at most lower fields (with the height as prominence 1 AP remains in the last 100 ms at 504 V/cm). Bleaching raises the inverted trace late in the AP-free sessions by 1.36 to 1.57%, which the O6 levels do not remove; with each neuron's AP-free late mean subtracted, a variant added after verification round 1, no neuron meets the criterion under any combination.
deviations: A neuron counts when most of its highest-field sessions show sustained depolarization, a standard choice; every highest field here has one session except subject 2 (2) and subject 4 (6).

outcomes.statement: Di-8-ANEPPS traces were noisier than FluoVolt traces, as the dye has a lower voltage sensitivity.
outcomes.source: Results, Sensitivity to unmodulated sine waves was not caused by FluoVolt dye, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Compared to FluoVolt recordings, the traces were expectedly noisier (Di-8-ANEPSS has a lower voltage sensitivity)
outcomes.notes: Changed from partially reproduced after verification round 1, since the criterion requires both measures and is met under none of the 12 readings, with either width bound and with the height as the dF value or as prominence. By the SD before the onset (reading b), the direct measure of noise, which does not depend on AP detection, the Di-8-ANEPPS traces are less noisy (whole frame 0.55 against 0.88%, p below 0.001; Otsu ROI 1.24 against 1.57 or 3.05%). By the signal to noise ratio (reading a) the Di-8-ANEPPS median is lower than the FluoVolt median under 10 of 12 readings with the height as the value and 6 of 12 as prominence (whole frame 7.0 to 9.7 against 12.7 to 12.9, t test p 0.001 to 0.14), because its median AP height is about half (3.7 to 6.7% against 10.1 to 14.5%; the FluoVolt value is near the paper's 11.3%). 3 Di-8-ANEPPS neurons against 20 to 27 FluoVolt neurons.
deviations: The FluoVolt group is the 2-kHz unmodulated 250-ms sessions of DANDI 001032, 001033 and 001035 (209 sessions, 28 neurons). DANDI 001034 is a byte-identical copy of 001032 (80 of 80 such sessions) and is counted once. DANDI 001030 holds only 2-s ramped waves in sodium gluconate and has no session the criterion admits.

outcomes.statement: Overall, the effects of 2-kHz sine waves in Di-8-ANEPPS neurons did not differ from those with FluoVolt, so the excitation by unmodulated sine waves is not a sensitization by FluoVolt.
outcomes.source: Results, Sensitivity to unmodulated sine waves was not caused by FluoVolt dye, paragraph 1; Discussion, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Overall, stimulation effects were not different from those observed with FluoVolt dye
outcomes.notes: Under unit reading (i) the t test finds no difference between the Di-8-ANEPPS (n = 2 or 3, mean 108 to 152 V/cm) and FluoVolt (n = 20 to 27, mean 140 to 178 V/cm) 1-AP thresholds under all 12 readings (p 0.27 to 0.98; difference -43 to 1 V/cm, 95% intervals as wide as -156 to 124 V/cm), nor with the height as prominence (p 0.15 to 0.64). Under reading (ii) the Di-8-ANEPPS thresholds are higher under 9 of 12 readings (p 0.002 to 0.017; 8 of 12 as prominence, 12 of 12 with the earlier 2-ms width bound). The response pattern holds only in part (figs1-near-threshold-delayed-aps not reproduced, figs1-stronger-field-shorter-delay-sustained-firing reproduced, figs1-culminates-in-sustained-depolarization not reproduced), so the criterion's condition for reproduced is not met; its condition for not reproduced, a threshold difference, is not met under the adopted unit reading either. The FluoVolt mean, about 150 V/cm, is far above the paper's 57.7 V/cm (reported, not judged); the one-sample tests of the Di-8-ANEPPS thresholds against 57.7 V/cm give p 0.14 to 0.36 with n = 2 or 3. With n = 2 or 3 and intervals this wide, the absence of a difference carries little information. The criterion gives no outcome for a pattern that fails with no threshold difference; this is asked of a reader in questions/001272.yaml. The change of figs1-near-threshold-delayed-aps to not reproduced in verification round 3 leaves this outcome as it is, as the pattern fails either way.
deviations: Assumed unit reading (i), the volts as the files state them times the files' 36 V/cm per volt in both groups. The 001032 to 001035 files call their volts peak-to-peak, and the 001272 files say only amplitude. In DANDI 001271, FluoVolt recorded in 2024 with the same wording as 001272, the 2-kHz thresholds (mean 3.70 V, n = 20) and those of 001032 to 001035 (4.20 V, n = 27) do not differ (p = 0.29). This gives no evidence against one scale but does not show the scales are equal, and the files say the delivered amplitude is smaller by a calibration that is not deposited. Reading (ii), FluoVolt volts halved, is shown.

outcomes.statement: Unmodulated 250-ms sine waves at 2 and 20 kHz excited every neuron tested, with APs 100 to 200 ms after onset near threshold, firing rate rising to a ceiling of 60 to 90 Hz, and an excitation block with sustained depolarization at the highest fields.
outcomes.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz unmodulated sine waves, paragraph 1; Figures 1A to 1C and inset
outcomes.quote: Pure sine waves at 2 and even 20 kHz excited 100% of neurons ... The maximum firing rate increased linearly until reaching a ceiling of 60-90 Hz
outcomes.notes: Answer to questions/001272.yaml on the O3 width. The claims file now takes an AP's width at half height between 1 and 20 ms, where it had 2 to 20 ms; re-run with 1 ms, the outcome is unchanged, and no reading meets the criterion with either bound, so the readings agree and the claim is not blocked. Measured values are those of the first reading (a/a/a), with the fraction for 2 kHz (with 2 ms they were 96.4, 41.15 and 78.63). Excitation is close to the claim under the whole frame (27 of 28 neurons at 2 kHz, 15 or 16 of 17 at 20 kHz; 8 to 17 of 17 at 20 kHz over all readings). Each reading fails one of the other two parts. The median over neurons of the highest first-two-AP rate is 25 to 177 Hz (whole frame 45 to 47 Hz, below the 54-Hz bound; 21 to 61 Hz with 2 ms), and the median first-AP latency at the lowest exciting field is 15 to 77 ms (whole frame 62 to 64 ms; 66 to 79 ms with 2 ms), below the 90-ms bound. Under a/a/a and a/b/a the rate, 63 Hz, is within its bounds, and the latency, 32 and 36 ms, is not; in the null test these readings detect 1.04 to 1.06 peaks per 100 ms after the stimulus and 1.07 to 1.10 before the onset, against 2.44 to 2.47 during it, and 20 in the 5 sham sessions. At most 1 of 32 neurons shows sustained depolarization at its highest field. Split by carrier, which the criterion's median does not do, the whole-frame latency is 49 ms at 2 kHz and 112 to 124 ms at 20 kHz. Leaving out the 38 sessions of 900 frames gives whole-frame rates of 47 to 49 Hz and latencies of 56 to 59 ms, and the height read as prominence gives rates of 39 to 43 Hz and latencies of 54 to 55 ms; no reading meets the criterion in either variant.
deviations: Data from DANDI 001032, 001033 and 001035, assigned to Figure 1 by the claims file from their titles; 001034 duplicates 001032 and is not used. 38 sessions have 900 frames and cover only 241 ms of the 250-ms stimulus.
The claims file's earlier AP width bound of 2 to 20 ms is run as a variant, to show what the reader's answer changed; it gives the same outcome.
outcomes.where: DANDI:001030 and 001032 to 001035 (assigned from their titles; the paper does not map figures to dandisets)

outcomes.statement: Responses to 20 kHz needed about 2-fold stronger fields than at 2 kHz, and all thresholds at 20 kHz were about 2-fold higher than at 2 kHz.
outcomes.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz unmodulated sine waves, paragraph 1; Results, Excitation thresholds are similar or lower, paragraph 1; Figure 2D
outcomes.quote: All thresholds at 20 kHz were about 2-fold higher than at 2 kHz ( p < 0.0001, two-tailed unpaired t test)
outcomes.notes: Answer to questions/001272.yaml on the O3 width. The claims file now takes an AP's width at half height between 1 and 20 ms, where it had 2 to 20 ms; re-run with 1 ms, the outcome is unchanged. No reading meets the criterion under (a) or (b), with either bound. The 20-kHz thresholds are higher than the 2-kHz ones (pooled p at most 1.4e-9; unmodulated groups p at most 0.003, below 0.0001 under the whole frame), but in every reading at least one ratio of means is outside 1.8 to 2.2. They range from 1.71 to 2.98 (1.88 to 2.86 with 2 ms); whole frame 2.27 to 2.39 for 1 AP and 2.41 to 2.44 for 5 APs unmodulated, 2.62 and 2.82 to 2.83 modulated. Under a/a/a the unmodulated ratios, 2.00 and 2.13, are within the range and the modulated ones, 2.77 and 2.98, are not. The modulated 20-kHz groups hold 1 to 3 neurons. Measured is the unmodulated 1-AP ratio of the first reading (2.16 with 2 ms).
deviations: Thresholds use the files' nominal volts; the files say the delivered amplitude is smaller by a frequency-dependent calibration that is not deposited, which bears directly on a 20 against 2 kHz ratio.

outcomes.statement: Thresholds for sine waves modulated at 20 Hz were significantly higher than for pure sine waves at the same carrier, for 5 APs at 2 kHz and for 1 and 5 APs at 20 kHz, so modulation did not lower excitation thresholds.
outcomes.source: Results, Excitation thresholds are similar or lower for pure 2- and 20-kHz sine waves than those for modulated sine waves, paragraph 1; Figure 2D
outcomes.quote: thresholds for modulated sine waves, which emulate the TI stimulus at the target, were significantly higher than those for pure sine waves at the same frequency ... p = 0.0079 ... p = 0.0142 and p = 0.0037
outcomes.notes: Answer to questions/001272.yaml on the O3 width. The claims file now takes an AP's width at half height between 1 and 20 ms, where it had 2 to 20 ms; re-run with 1 ms, the outcome is unchanged. No reading meets the criterion, with either bound, so the readings agree. Modulated thresholds are higher in every group with data, but the 2-kHz 5-AP difference is not significant under any reading (p 0.0500 to 0.93; 0.085 to 0.48 with 2 ms). Under whole/a/a and whole/b/a the other three parts hold and this p, 0.0500, is at the bound and not below it, so the outcome is close to the criterion there. The 20-kHz modulated groups hold 1 to 3 neurons (1 AP p 0.0005 to 0.87; 5 APs p 0.0096 to 0.058 where computable). The 2-kHz 1-AP threshold is not lower for modulated waves (higher, p 0.023 to 0.75).

outcomes.statement: With 20-Hz modulation, firing above threshold locked to the beats, one AP near the peak of each of the five beats and at most two per beat (ten in all), and modulated sine waves triggered no sustained firing or sustained depolarization.
outcomes.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz sinusoids modulated at 20 Hz, paragraph 1; Figures 2A and 2B
outcomes.quote: single APs emerged near the peak of each beat, so the firing rate equaled the modulation rate ... the maximum number of APs evoked by five beats was limited to ten. Unlike pure sine waves, modulated stimuli did not trigger sustained firing or sustained depolarization
outcomes.notes: Answer to questions/001272.yaml on the O3 width. The claims file now takes an AP's width at half height between 1 and 20 ms, where it had 2 to 20 ms; re-run with 1 ms, the outcome is unchanged, but the criterion is now met under fewer readings and fails under the adopted whole frame for a different reason. Locking holds under every reading. In most sessions with 5 or more APs most fall 12.5 to 37.5 ms into the 50-ms beat (whole frame 22 of 25 or 23 of 26 sessions; 66 to 100% of all APs there over readings, 89 to 91% under the whole frame), and the whole-frame phase histogram peaks 20 to 35 ms into the beat while that of unmodulated sessions is flat. The criterion is met under 4 of 12 readings, the Otsu-ROI readings with height (b) (8 of 12 with 2 ms). Under the Otsu ROI with the 5% height 10 to 20 modulated sessions have more than 10 APs (up to 17), readings that detect 20 APs in 5 sham sessions. Under the 4 whole-frame readings one modulated session (001032 neuron 10_1, 2 kHz, 8 V) has 13 APs, against 17 in the neuron's unmodulated session at that field, and no modulated session shows sustained depolarization. With 2 ms the whole-frame readings failed instead on sustained depolarization by O6 level (a) in one session, with no session over 10 APs, and so do they with the height read as prominence (at most 9 APs; met under 4 of 12 readings). The null test of the detector finds 0.09 to 0.10 peaks per 100 ms after the stimulus under the whole frame, against 1.77 to 1.83 during it, and under the Otsu ROI with the 5% height 1.04 to 1.06 (ROI a, against 2.44 to 2.47 during) and 2.12 to 2.14 (ROI b, against 3.33 to 3.38). The statement's "no sustained firing" is not tested by the criterion; the O6 sustained-firing rule is met by beat-locked firing (45 or 46 of 84 modulated sessions under the whole frame), and a reader is asked in questions/001272.yaml whether the criterion should test it.
deviations: Assumed the whole deposited frame as the soma ROI where the ROI readings disagree (here and in fig3c-sustained-firing-2s and figs2-ttx-blocks-depolarization). The Methods measure "the emission over the entire cell soma"; the deposited 16 x 16 frames are a crop around the soma, the claims file's Otsu ROI keeps one membrane edge only, and with the 5% height it detects 5 APs in the 5 sham sessions of DANDI 001271, where the whole frame detects none.
The beat peak is taken 25 ms into each 50-ms beat, as the criterion says; the files do not store the stimulus waveform.

outcomes.statement: In the same neuron at the same field strength, pure sine waves triggered more APs than modulated ones, and the threshold was typically lower for unmodulated signals.
outcomes.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz sinusoids modulated at 20 Hz, paragraph 2; Figures 2A to 2C
outcomes.quote: the threshold was typically lower for unmodulated signals ( Figures 2A - 2C ). At the same field strengths, pure sine waves triggered a larger number of APs
outcomes.notes: Answer to questions/001272.yaml on the O3 width. The claims file now takes an AP's width at half height between 1 and 20 ms, where it had 2 to 20 ms; re-run with 1 ms, the outcome is unchanged. Under all 12 readings, with either bound, unmodulated waves evoke more APs than modulated ones at the same neuron, carrier and field in more of the 52 pairs than the reverse (22 to 47 against 0 to 12; paired t test p from below 0.0001 to 0.022), and the unmodulated threshold is lower in more neurons than the reverse (9 to 14 against 0 to 2). The same holds under all 12 readings with the height read as prominence.

outcomes.statement: Lowering solution conductivity from 16.4 to 8.4 mS/cm with sodium gluconate reversibly lowered excitation thresholds about 2-fold at all sine wave frequencies from 2 to 20 kHz.
outcomes.source: Results, Decreased extracellular conductivity lowers excitation thresholds, paragraph 1; Figures 3A and 3B
outcomes.quote: Switching to the NaGlu-based solution reversibly and reproducibly decreased excitation thresholds ~2-fold across all sine wave frequencies tested
outcomes.notes: No deposit holds the data. The claim needs 1-AP thresholds for 250-ms unmodulated sine waves at 2 to 20 kHz in both NaCl and sodium gluconate solution. No file read of DANDI 001032, 001033, 001035 and 001271 mentions gluconate (0 of the 454 2- and 20-kHz files of 001032, 001033 and 001035, 0 of the 287 of 001271; the other files of these deposits are at other frequencies and were not read), 001030 holds only 2-s ramped 2-kHz waves in sodium gluconate (17 files), and 001031 holds 100-kHz bipolar pulses. The paper names no other deposit. This would be data_missing, which the registry's check does not allow for a claim marked elsewhere.
outcomes.where: DANDI:001030 and 001032 to 001035 (assigned from their titles)

outcomes.statement: In the low-conductivity solution, a 2-s unmodulated 2-kHz sine wave ramped over 250 ms evoked firing for its whole duration, rising with field until replaced by a firing block with sustained depolarization.
outcomes.source: Results, Decreased extracellular conductivity lowers excitation thresholds, paragraph 3; Figure 3C
outcomes.quote: we observed sustained firing for the entire duration of the sine wave ( Figure 3C ). The rate of firing increased with the electric field strength until it was replaced by a firing block and sustained depolarization
outcomes.notes: Answer to questions/001272.yaml on the O3 width. The claims file now takes an AP's width at half height between 1 and 20 ms, where it had 2 to 20 ms; re-run with 1 ms, the outcome is unchanged. The pattern is present in neuron c7 of DANDI 001030. Under the whole frame with the AP height taken as prominence it fires through the 2-s wave at 1.45 to 2.0 V (75 to 91 APs, 8 to 10 in the last 250 ms), and at 2.3 V fires 19 APs, none in the last 250 ms, with a late dF of 6.0% against 5.4% or less at lower fields; it meets all three parts. Under the whole frame c7's 1.0-V session is the only session without APs, so the two bleaching corrections subtract the same trace from c7's sessions and are one check for c7, not two. With the height as the dF value, 9 detections in the last 250 ms at 2.3 V count as firing and c7 fails. A null test on 001030, added after verification round 2, does not decide between the height readings. Under the whole frame neither detects a peak in the 25 ms before the onset, and after the stimulus, where the trace is back near baseline, the value reading detects none and prominence 0 to 7 (up to 0.24 per 100 ms, against 1.85 to 2.60 during the stimulus). The 9 late detections at 2.3 V have prominences of 1.9 to 4.4%, below the 4.43% threshold, but the session's earlier detections have prominences of 1.3 to 19.1% (median 4.0%), so prominence does not set the late ones apart by size. The outcome rests on the prominence reading, supported by the figure of the traces (a flat plateau at 2.3 V) and the verifier's synthetic test, and not confirmed by a null test. No reading has more than 1 of the 4 neurons meeting the criterion (at most 2 with 2 ms, when c8 also met it under the shared correction), and no Otsu-ROI reading has any. c5 and c6 were stimulated up to 2.0 and 1.45 V only and keep firing; two c5 files end at 1,913 ms, before the stimulus ends.
deviations: The Methods subtract "a trace without APs" for bleaching without saying which. Two readings are run, each neuron's own lowest-field session when it has no AP (only c7's has none), and the dataset's one AP-free 2-s session subtracted from all others.
The criterion does not say whether the pattern is judged per neuron or in the representative neuron of Figure 3C. It is judged per neuron here, and the outcome is partial as it holds in 1 or 2 of 4.

Assumed the AP height read as prominence, as a depolarized baseline makes noise peaks pass a height measured as the dF value; the verifier's synthetic test (a 5.5% plateau with 0.5% noise gives 6 false APs with the value, 0 with prominence) shows the mechanism.
The O6 window is the last 250 ms of the stimulus, as this claims file's criterion gives it.

outcomes.statement: 1 uM tetrodotoxin abolished both the APs and the sustained depolarization caused by intense unmodulated 2-kHz sine waves, while the vehicle did not.
outcomes.source: Results, Tetrodotoxin blocks sustained depolarization, paragraph 1; Figure S2 legend
outcomes.quote: the inhibition of sodium channels with 1 μM tetrodotoxin not only abolished the APs but also fully blocked the sustained depolarization
outcomes.notes: Answer to questions/001272.yaml on the O3 width. The claims file now takes an AP's width at half height between 1 and 20 ms, where it had 2 to 20 ms; re-run with 1 ms, the outcome is unchanged. Under the 4 whole-frame readings and the Otsu-ROI readings with height (b), with either bound, APs present before TTX are absent after in every TTX neuron of DANDI 001271 (whole/a/b, 20 to 94 APs before, 0 after, at 4 to 6 matched fields in all 6), and every vehicle neuron with matched fields keeps firing (13 of 13 under the whole frame). Under the Otsu ROI with the 5% height, 1 to 4 TTX neurons keep detections after TTX, the readings that also detect 20 APs in 5 sham sessions. The criterion's second part is conditional (sustained depolarization present before is absent after). Sustained depolarization before TTX is found in only 1 of 6 TTX neurons (14_20240731), and is absent after; the other 5 do not test that part, and no TTX neuron has a late mean dF above 5% before. After TTX the late dF is -0.38 to -0.70% in every TTX neuron, against 0.12 to 3.28% before. So the APs part is tested in 6 neurons and the sustained-depolarization part in 1. With the height read as prominence, a variant, 3 or 4 of the 6 TTX neurons keep detections after TTX under the whole frame (1 to 6 each under whole/a/b); that reading detects 1 or 2 peaks in the 5 sham sessions, where the value reading detects none. The record uses prominence for fig3c-sustained-firing-2s and the value reading here; under prominence this claim would fail. A reader is asked in questions/001272.yaml whether the criterion should require sustained depolarization before TTX, which the conditional criterion lets pass when it is absent.
deviations: Nothing in the files marks when the vehicle was added; for vehicle neurons the largest gap between consecutive sessions (0.6 to 10.8 min) is taken as the change. One vehicle neuron (17_20240801) has no field in common across the gap and is not counted.
The ROI is the whole frame, as assumed for fig2-modulated-locks-to-beats.

outcomes.statement: Membrane charging by 2-us pulses is fast; pooled over 19 experiments, charging and discharging time constants averaged 0.7 and 0.91 us at the cathodic pole and 0.65 and 0.8 us at the anodic pole, so membranes charge fully within each sine wave cycle up to 100 to 200 kHz.
outcomes.source: Results, Kinetics of membrane charging by pulsed electric fields, the paragraph after the Figure 4 legend; Figures 4D and 4E
outcomes.quote: The time constants pooled together for all cells averaged 0.7 ± 0.08 (charging) and 0.91 ± 0.08 (discharging) μs for the cathodic cell pole and 0.65 ± 0.05 and 0.8 ± 0.07 μs for the anodic pole, respectively (mean ± SEM, n = 19)
outcomes.notes: Changed from blocked after verification round 1. The criterion defers to the DANDI 001273 claims file, whose header (F2) runs the fits unscaled where the debris ROI is not available, so the claim is testable; all 22 experiments are now fitted under every reading (001273-O1 ROI a and b, O2 weighting, O3 discharge amplitude). No reading gives all four mean time constants within the paper's SEMs (0 of 8; 0 of 8 also with the whole-frame scaling variant), so the readings agree. Charging means are near the paper's under some readings (cathodic 0.68 to 1.27 us against 0.7 +/- 0.08, anodic 0.64 to 0.77 us against 0.65 +/- 0.05); discharging means are higher (cathodic 1.30 to 2.35 us against 0.91 +/- 0.08, anodic 0.91 to 2.62 us against 0.8 +/- 0.07), and the SEMs over experiments (0.13 to 0.65 us) are larger than the paper's. The traces are noisy, the dF late in the pulse a median 1.97 times the SD before it (0.16 to 8.37). Of 352 unscaled fits, 58 charging and 15 discharging time constants end at a fit bound and are left out; none failed to converge. Measured values are those of the first reading (ROI a, unweighted, free discharge amplitude), in the order of the expected values. The missing debris scaling may account for the difference.
deviations: Unscaled fits, as the 001273 claims file's F2 gives when the debris ROI is not available; the debris ROI is not deposited. Scaling by the whole-frame mean is shown as a variant.
The mean is over the 22 groups of 7 or 8 replicates of one cell, electrode orientation and amplitude in the files, where the paper reports 19 experiments, with no mapping between them.
Fits with a time constant within 1% of a fit bound (0.01 or 20 us) are counted as failed and left out of the mean, a standard choice; their number is reported.
The ROIs are rebuilt from the RATIO image under the 001273 claims file's O1 readings; the cell is the largest Otsu component of the filtered CONTROL image, a standard choice.

outcomes.statement: Aligning elongated cells with the field doubled the time constants; the maximum optical TMP and the time constants did not differ between the cathode- and anode-facing poles; and discharging was slower than charging except in elongated cells aligned with the field.
outcomes.source: Results, Kinetics of membrane charging by pulsed electric fields, the paragraph after the Figure 4 legend; Figures 4D and 4E
outcomes.quote: Δ F max did not differ at the cathodic and anodic cell poles, indicating the lack of rectification of the applied electric field ... Aligning elongated cells with the electric field doubled the time constants ... discharging time constants were always larger than the charging ones in the same cell ( p < 0.001, paired t test)
outcomes.notes: The criterion needs all three of fig4-orientation-time-constants, fig4-no-pole-difference and fig4-discharging-slower of the DANDI 001273 claims file. The orientation part needs the cell-shape groups (elongated parallel, elongated perpendicular, random), which the files do not label (they give the electrode positions only, up and bottom for 83 files, right and left for 35, not specified for 63). The other two parts were run on the unscaled fits of fig4-pooled-time-constants and are reported. No pole difference is found in |dFmax|, charging tau or discharging tau under any of the 8 readings (paired p 0.25 to 0.98, n = 15 to 21), as the claim says. Discharging tau is larger than charging tau under every reading (by 0.52 to 1.56 us) but not at p below 0.001 (p 0.0013 to 0.22) over all experiments and both poles, the 001273 criterion's reading (a); its readings (b) and (c) and the exception for elongated parallel cells need the groups.

outcomes.statement: FluoVolt sensitivity to 2-kHz sine waves (11.8% per 1 kV/cm) was 42% of that to 2-us pulses (28% per 1 kV/cm) and smaller in every ROI, with sine waves polarizing the two poles more asymmetrically than pulses.
outcomes.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, paragraphs 2 to 5; Figures 5, 6B to 6D and S3
outcomes.quote: All numbers were invariably smaller than those measured for the same ROIs with the pulse ( Figure 6D ). The electric field sensitivity averaged across all ROIs in all the cells was 11.8% ± 1.7% per 1 kV/cm, just 42% of the value for the 2-μs pulses
outcomes.notes: Not attempted in this run. The criterion defers to five claims of the DANDI 001274 claims file (26 claims), whose measures need ROIs on 512 x 512 strobe images of nine cells, with and without scaling to a debris ROI. The data are not too large (232 files, 25 GB, which stream at about 25 MB/s). The same kind of strobe recordings in DANDI 001273 could not be fitted without the debris ROI (strobe_check.ipynb); whether the larger pulse and sine-wave signals of Figures 5 and 6 survive without it was not checked here, and the run stopped short of the nine-cell analysis.

outcomes.statement: The 2-kHz AP threshold of 57.7 V/cm times the sine wave sensitivity gives a 0.68% emission change, about 6.8 mV, so the threshold depolarization is 5 to 15 mV, as with intracellular current injection.
outcomes.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, last paragraph
outcomes.quote: This threshold corresponds to a 0.68% ± 0.11% FluoVolt emission change (11.8 × 57.7/1,000) ... a 0.68% emission change corresponds to a 6.8-mV depolarization at the AP threshold
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig6-sine-less-than-pulse, blocked. Its first expected value, the mean unmodulated 2-kHz 1-AP threshold (57.7 +/- 3.6 V/cm), is measured in fluovolt_elsewhere.ipynb as 151.2 V/cm under the whole-frame reading and 140 to 178 V/cm over all readings, with the files' nominal volts and 36 V/cm per volt; the files say the delivered amplitude is smaller by a calibration that is not deposited.
outcomes.where: DANDI:001032 to 001035 for the threshold and DANDI:001274 for the sensitivity (assigned from their titles)

findings.statement: The dataset holds 3 neurons recorded with Di-8-ANEPPS (subjects 2, 3 and 4 of 2024-08-06), where the paper reports 8 for this experiment (Figure S1).
None of the paper's ten deposits holds the 250-ms sine wave sessions in sodium gluconate solution behind Figure 3B; 001030 holds only 2-s ramped waves in that solution.

DANDI 001034 appears to duplicate DANDI 001032. All 80 of its 2-kHz unmodulated files have frame stacks identical to those of 001032, under subject names ending in _3 in place of _1; its other files were not compared.

Every file of DANDI 001272 (65 of 65) describes the session as performed "without tetrodotoxin (vehicle control)", wording taken from the tetrodotoxin experiment (001271); the Di-8-ANEPPS experiment had no tetrodotoxin arm.

The tetrodotoxin sessions of DANDI 001271 (71 of 71) describe tetrodotoxin as one "which abolished the action potentials and caused sustained depolarization during application of stimulating waves". The paper says it blocked the sustained depolarization, and in the data the late dF after tetrodotoxin is -0.38 to -0.70% in all 6 neurons.

The stimulus onset is not stored in DANDI 001272 or 001271 (the Methods put it at 50 ms; the responses are consistent with that, peaking in an onset contrast at 50 ms), and no file stores the stimulus waveform or the field in V/cm other than as text in the session description.

Amplitudes are given in volts with inconsistent meaning. DANDI 001032 to 001035 call them peak-to-peak, 001030 and 001031 one polarity ("peak-to-peak would be two-fold larger"), and 001272 and 001271 say neither, yet all apply the same 36 V/cm per volt. The files also say the delivered amplitude is smaller by a frequency-dependent calibration "to be reported separately", which is not deposited. With the stated conversion the mean 2-kHz FluoVolt threshold is about 150 V/cm, against the paper's 57.7 V/cm.

The frames are 16 x 16 pixels where the Methods give 64 x 64 after binning, and nothing says which part of the sensor they are or how the soma region was drawn, so the paper's soma ROI cannot be reproduced.

Frame 0 of every DANDI 001272 file is 1.7 to 15.7 times brighter than the median frame, a camera artefact that must be dropped before computing F0. 33 of 62 intervals between consecutive sessions are under the 20 s the Methods give (range 4 to 168 s).

Questions for the paper's authors. (1) Was the soma emission F taken over the whole deposited 16 x 16 frame, and if not, over what region? (2) For Di-8-ANEPPS, what AP height, measured from what baseline, and what delay after onset count as an AP and as "delayed"? (3) Are the 001272 amplitudes peak-to-peak like those of 001032 to 001035, and what were the delivered amplitudes? (4) Which trace without APs was subtracted from the 2-s recordings of Figure 3C? (5) When was the vehicle added in the vehicle neurons of 001271? This attempt assumed the whole frame, a height of 5 SD of the pre-stimulus trace measured as the peak's prominence for Di-8-ANEPPS, a delay of at least 100 ms, the stated volts on one scale, and the largest gap between sessions.

DANDI 001273 does not hold the debris ROI the paper scales its strobe images to, nor the ROIs over the cell poles, nor the cell-shape groups of Figure 4. Without the scaling, laser-flash fluctuation of the order of the signal dominates the replicate-mean traces. The files form 22 experiments of 7 or 8 replicates, one pair and 4 single files, where the paper reports 19, with no mapping.

In DANDI 001273, 164 of the 175 replicates fitted have at least one dark frame (257 in all, 0.34 to 0.80 of the median frame mean), in 95 of them only the first acquired frame. They are left out of the fits.
The paper lists ten dandisets for its raw images without saying which figure each holds; the claims file and this attempt assign them from their titles.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The three executed notebooks with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper modules, and the paper. The claims file the verifier was given was the one for DANDI:001273, not claims/001272/10.1016-j.xcrp.2025.102660.yaml (the handover copies every claims file of the paper under its file name, and the two share one), and it had no attempt record. It judged the claims the two files share against the 001273 criteria, and the 001272-only Figure S1 claims against the criteria as the notebook quotes them. The results below are for the claims of this attempt; where the verifier judged a claim under the 001273 file, its reason is given and the response says where the criteria differ. Its claims figs1-di8-anepps-control, fig5-sine-asymmetry and the separate fig4 claims of the 001273 file are not claims of this attempt; figs1-di8-anepps-control is covered by the Figure S1 claims above, and the fig4 parts by fig4-orientation-and-poles.

disagreements.reason: methods_underspecified. The readings disagree, it passes under 19 of 48 combinations (cell 16).
The latency part holds in 3 of 3 neurons under most readings. The sustained-firing part rests on AP counts under height (b), which include noise (problem 4).

The pattern part already fails (culminates). The threshold comparison depends on the amplitude scale, no difference in 12 of 12 readings on the files' scale, a difference in 9 of 12 with FluoVolt halved.

Under the file's AP readings (peak value), no neuron's top-field session has no late APs together with elevated dF. The top sessions either have late APs (c7, 9) or a late mean <= 3.3% (cell 20). This holds under both bleaching corrections. The notebook takes the last 250 ms with the O6 levels; the provided file says "after 250 ms" at 5% (problem 10).

Under whole-frame readings, APs are abolished in 6 of 6 TTX neurons and kept in 13 of 13 vehicle neurons (cell 23). The criterion also needs a late mean dF above 5% before TTX; the observed values are 0.12-3.28%, so the depolarization part fails. The notebook's pass is vacuous on that part (problem 2).

Not reproduced for the threshold part; the rest untested. The FluoVolt 2-kHz mean 1-AP threshold is 140-178 V/cm with the files' scale, or 70-89 V/cm with it halved (di8 cell 26). Neither is within 57.7 +/- 3.6 V/cm. The sensitivity terms need DANDI:001274, which was not loaded. Calibration caveat in problem 7.

methods_underspecified, likely. Shape labels are not needed for this claim, and a missing debris ROI only makes the analysis "unscaled, as a deviation" (header F2), so the notebook's metadata_insufficient reason does not hold. The real obstacles are 22 experiments where the paper reports 19, and fits that vary widely across readings on the one experiment run (problem 8).

verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The three full executed notebooks with their conclusions and summaries, the helper modules, the claims file for this dataset (claims/001272/10.1016-j.xcrp.2025.102660.yaml), the attempt record with its round-1 entry, and the paper.

disagreements.reason: The two assumptions are stated; prominence is well founded (null test 0.02 against 1.43 per 100 ms) and O5 (a) has a source in the paper. But under those assumptions the criterion is met in 0 of 24 combinations under O5 (a) (cell 20), only 1 of 3 neurons qualifies, and more than half are needed. The criterion is one per-neuron test that needs "1-3 APs" and "delayed" together and does not split into parts, so the outcome under the assumptions is not_reproduced. "Partially" only describes the halves of that test.

entries.name: 001048-semenov-2025
entries.title: High-frequency sine waves excite isolated neurons (Semenov et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Semenov, Kim, Silkuniene and Pakhomov (2025). Dandiset 001048 names the paper but holds HEK-cell recordings of another study, so the claims are tested on the ten dandisets the paper lists (001030 to 001035, 001271 to 001274). These hold optical recordings of rat hippocampal neurons stimulated by unmodulated and 20-Hz modulated sine waves at 2 and 20 kHz, with TTX and Di-8-ANEPPS controls, and strobe images of membrane charging by 2-us pulses and sine waves.

entries.name: 001271-semenov-2025
entries.title: Sine wave excitation and tetrodotoxin in isolated neurons (Semenov et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the Figure S2 findings of Semenov, Kim, Silkuniene and Pakhomov (2025) on dandiset 001271, which holds optical membrane potential recordings of 20 cultured hippocampal neurons stimulated by 250-ms, 2-kHz sine waves before and after the solution was replaced by one with tetrodotoxin (6 neurons) or without it (vehicle). Two more notebooks test findings the paper deposited in other dandisets, Figure 3C on 001030 and Figures 1, 2 and S1 on 001032 to 001035 and 001272. The adiabatic heating estimate is recomputed from the paper's values. The strobe imaging of Figures 4 to 6 (001273, 001274) is not tested.

entries.description: Tests the Figure 4 findings of Semenov, Kim, Silkuniene and Pakhomov (2025) on dandiset 001273, which holds the pulsed laser strobe imaging of FluoVolt-loaded rat hippocampal neurons exposed to 2-us pulses. It rebuilds the RATIO image and the polarized ROIs of the Methods, fits the charging and discharging time constants, and checks where the poles lie against the field axis. Two more notebooks test the 2-s sine wave recordings of Figure 3C (dandiset 001030) and the Di-8-ANEPPS recordings of Figure S1 (dandiset 001272). The paper's other figures, in other dandisets, are not tested; a fourth notebook surveys those dandisets' metadata.

entries.description: Tests the findings of Semenov, Kim, Silkuniene and Pakhomov (2025) on dandiset 001274, which holds the strobe images of membrane polarization by pulses and sine waves (Figures 5, 6 and S3), and on the other dandisets of the same paper that hold the fast optical recordings of action potentials (001030, 001032, 001033, 001035, 001271, 001272).
